national.basis: Our division: Statistics Finland's passenger-car traffic volume on Finnish streets and roads (12jx) divided by passenger cars in traffic use at the end of the same year (11ie). The volume also counts foreign cars driving in Finland and leaves out Finnish cars abroad, and the fleet is a year-end count, so this is an approximation. Rounded to the km.

byPowertrainFromInspections.basis: Traficom's average and median odometer reading at the 2025 periodic inspection, by motive power and vehicle age. medianKmPerYearOfAge = medianKm / ageYears, rounded to 100 km: the average yearly km over the car's life so far, not last year's km. Survivors only (cars still in use), and buyers who drive a lot choose diesel, so do not read the gap as caused by the fuel. Rows under 100 inspections are left out.

kmPerYear.gap: No official per-car yearly km by fuel was found (Traficom and Statistics Finland publish totals, fleet counts and odometer readings, not km per car per year by fuel).

consumption.rule: Use the ad's own combined consumption (yhdistetty kulutus) when it gives one. The figures below only adjust an official WLTP value to real-world use; they are not a consumption to assume for a car.

realWorldGapWLTP.year: new cars first registered in 2021, first year of use (EU-wide OBFCM data)
realWorldGapWLTP.quote: the real-world fuel consumption experienced by drivers remains on average 1-1.5 l/100km higher than what is indicated on the official documents
realWorldGapWLTP.caveats: Applies to WLTP values only (cars type-approved under WLTP, roughly first registered from 2019 on). The old NEDC gap had grown to around 40 % by 2017 (same report). Heavy cars (SUVs, luxury) have a gap 1.5–2.5 times larger in g/km. The plug-in hybrid figure depends on how often the car is charged. No gap for electric cars is in the report.

consumption.gap: No official Finnish fleet-average consumption by fuel, and no official real-world gap for electric cars, was found. Leave consumption empty when the ad gives none.

traficom.what: Traficom keeps a database of recall campaigns reported to it (ajoneuvolaki 82/2021): cars, vans, motorcycles, mopeds, tractors, trailers and more, active and closed. Minor service or repair campaigns need not be reported and are not in it. Safety Gate notifications from 2021 and 2022 are missing from it; Traficom lists them in a separate PDF.

counts.basis: Counts as the database's search returned them on the date; it covers 2002 onward.

traficom.fields: make and vehicle type, model text (free text, e.g. 'Octavia, Karoq, Superb, Kodiaq'), fault, fault description, start and end date, campaign code, number of vehicles in Finland, the company running the campaign and an EC type-approval number. No structured model years; years appear only in some descriptions.

linkPatterns.notes: From the site's own routes. 'keyword' searches the text fields (model names match; 'Octavia' gave 25 campaigns). '2' is the vehicle type Henkilöauto; makeId is the site's id for a make (e.g. Audi 5, BMW 7) from its make list. The keyword link is the simplest for the app: 'Check recalls for this model' → keyword = the model name from the ad.

traficom.openData: None found. The database is not on Traficom's open-data list (which gives CC BY 4.0 for the vehicle register and other listed datasets). The site reads its own JSON endpoint (/api/recall), which is undocumented and comes with no licence or terms of reuse.

safetyGate.what: The EU rapid alert system for dangerous non-food products. Its 'Motor vehicles' category holds recalls notified by EU/EEA authorities. Of the 3,048 passenger-car alerts from October 2016 to October 2026, Germany notified 1,826 and France 610; Finland none. Traficom's database page points to Safety Gate for recall details in other languages.
safetyGate.openData: Weekly reports since 2005 as XML and Excel; data.europa.eu lists the XML and Excel distributions under CC0 and the search pages under the Commission's reuse policy (CC BY 4.0). Pictures may contain third-party rights and are not copied.

verdict.snapshotBuilt: car-recalls-eu.json: Safety Gate passenger-car alerts from 2016-10-01, built by tools/recalls-snapshot.mjs. Legally clear (CC0) and practical (one file, no server). Limit: it is EU-wide, not 'sold in Finland', and it has production dates, not Finnish registration years.
verdict.traficomSnapshot: Not built. It is practical (one JSON endpoint, about 2,800 car campaigns), but no licence or reuse terms are published for this database, its endpoint is undocumented, and each record names a contact person at the importer, which we must not copy. Ask Traficom (tietojenluovutus@traficom.fi, the contact on its open-data page) whether the database may be reused and under which licence before snapshotting it. Until then, link to it with the keyword pattern.
verdict.appCanShowNow: A 'Check recalls for this model' link to Traficom's search with the ad's model as keyword, and, from the EU snapshot, alerts whose make matches and whose years overlap the car's year, each with its Safety Gate link.
